business_scope.primary_industry_name: Long-Haul Bonded Highway Freight Transport under TIR Carnets

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition codified in the Swiss Civil Code and Swiss Code of Obligations)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Switzerland–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 27 January 1986; entered into force 18 March 1988)
Agreement between the Swiss Confederation and the European Community on the Carriage of Goods and Passengers by Road (Land Transport Agreement, 21 June 1999)
Customs Convention on the International Transport of Goods under Cover of TIR Carnets (TIR Convention, Geneva, 14 November 1975)
Convention on the Contract for the International Carriage of Goods by Road (CMR, Geneva, 19 May 1956)
Active Swiss network of double taxation agreements (DTAAs) covering principal transit jurisdictions: Germany, France, Italy, Austria, Netherlands, Luxembourg, United Kingdom, United States

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA/GwG, SR 955.0); Swiss Criminal Code Arts. 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Persons and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (Transparency Act, SR 221.419, effective 1 November 2023) and implementing Beneficial Owners Ordinance; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411); FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.03)
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (central UBO register accessible to MROS, FINMA, prosecution authorities and AMLA-obligated financial intermediaries; not publicly searchable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarial public deed of incorporation and Articles of Association (Statuten) under Art. 640 of the Swiss Code of Obligations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Duly appointed Swiss cantonal notary public in the canton of the registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization for Swiss Commercial Register filing; Hague Apostille by the competent cantonal authority only if the deed must be produced abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Apostilled certified copy of passport of each director, shareholder and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the relevant State plus competent Apostille authority (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Convention States)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (12 States Party) OR Consular Legalization via Swiss consular post for non-contracting States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of residence / police clearance certificate (Criminal Record Extract) of each natural-person director and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, followed by certified translation into German, French or Italian

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Current extract from the foreign commercial or company register of every corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign companies registry or competent judicial authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, with certified translation into an official Swiss language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner transparency declaration (e-UBO filing per Transparency Act Art. 10) signed by the incorporators
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company representatives before the Swiss notary / via the cantonal commercial register electronic filing dialogue
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization integrated in the incorporation deed; no separate apostille for domestic filing

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, beneficial owners and authorized signatories against: (1) UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (2) Swiss SECO state-issued sanctions and embargo lists; (3) FINMA enforcement and prohibition lists; (4) OFAC SDN and Consolidated Sanctions List (applicable given USD wire and fuel-card clearing rails); and (5) Swiss MROS typology expectations. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are subject to enhanced due diligence under Art. 4(2) AMLA, including source-of-wealth verification and senior-management approval before share transfer or director appointment.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: ZEFIX (Zentraler Firmenindex / Central Business Name Index, zefix.ch), maintained by the Federal Commercial Register Office, with filing and preliminary name clarification conducted through the competent cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) of the canton of the registered office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Arts. 950 and 954 of the Swiss Code of Obligations and Art. 54 HRegV, the corporate name must be truthful and non-misleading and may be in German, French, Italian or Romansh. A name in a non-official language (e.g., English) is permitted where the undertaking has an international business scope, provided the name can be pronounced in at least one official Swiss language and is not deceptive. The token 'TIR' in the proposed name requires supporting evidence of IRU (International Road Transport Union) authorization as a TIR Carnet holder; otherwise the register will treat it as misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banque, Banker, Börse — requires FINMA banking license
Insurance, Assurance, Assekuranz — requires FINMA insurance license
Swiss, Suisse, Svizzera — requires compliance with Swissness legislation (Trade Mark Act Art. 47 et seq.; majority Swiss control and administration)
Trust, Treuhand, Fiduciary — misleading implication of licensed fiduciary activity
Holding — requires qualifying holding-company economic substance
Foundation, Stiftung — requires cantonal supervisory approval
Confederation, Federal, Eidgenossenschaft, Cantonal — reserved for state entities
TIR — protected IRU trademark; prior IRU accreditation and TIR Carnet authorization evidence required
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant obtains a preliminary binding name clarification (Vorabklärung) from the cantonal Commercial Register Office under Art. 23 HRegV, valid for 180 days. Upon expiry, the applicant may submit a fresh clarification request; no automatic extension exists. If the name is rejected by formal ruling, the applicant may: (1) amend the proposed name and resubmit; (2) file a written administrative objection with the cantonal commercial register supervisory authority designated for the relevant canton, within the statutory appeal period (typically 30 days from notification); and (3) pursue further judicial review before the cantonal administrative court and ultimately the Federal Supreme Court on issues of federal commercial register law. The appeal must state the grounds and attach the contested ruling and supporting evidence of non-deception.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure mailbox or virtual office is not acceptable as the sole registered office (Sitz) of an operating Aktiengesellschaft engaged in TIR trucking. The registered office must correspond to the place where the company's administration is effectively conducted, and at least one director or authorized signatory must be resident in Switzerland (Art. 718 CO). A physically equipped shared administrative office or business center in the registered canton is permissible provided the company maintains real presence, statutory records, and operational management functions there. A letterbox-only arrangement will be rejected at registration and would also jeopardize the freight transport license and EU establishment criteria under EU Regulation 1071/2009.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Low at the pre-incorporation stage (<5% probability of an unannounced visit during the first six months). Once licensed by the Federal Roads Office (FEDRO/ASTRA) for commercial goods transport, unannounced establishment and good-repute inspections occur with an estimated annual probability of 15–25% for cross-border TIR operators, in line with EU Regulation 1071/2009 enforcement practice.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preliminary name clearance and binding name reservation (Vorabklärung) at the cantonal Commercial Register Office (illustrative FX: 1.00 CHF = 1.15 USD)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory cantonal tariff; approximate CHF 60–120 per name clarification request

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial public deed of incorporation (Art. 640 CO), including drafting of Articles of Association and UBO transparency declarations
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff scaled on registered share capital (CHF 100,000 minimum), prevailing market range CHF 1,500–3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First registration entry fee in the Swiss Commercial Register (Handelsregistereintrag) including electronic filing portal surcharge
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee under the Commercial Register Fee Ordinance (HRegGebV) with cantonal multiplier; approximate CHF 700–900

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official publication of the incorporation in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB)
Central UBO register initial e-filing and beneficial owner declaration processing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office / Central UBO Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No separate statutory fee; administrative cost absorbed in the registration fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille or Consular Legalization of foreign passport copies, criminal record certificates, and corporate registry extracts, plus certified translation into an official Swiss language
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal apostille authority or Swiss consular post, plus certified translation providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document fee (approximately CHF 30–50 per apostille) plus prevailing translation market rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and administrative substance service for the first year (physical office presence, statutory records custody, mail and authority liaison)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed fiduciary, law firm, or business center provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; CHF 1,500–2,500 per annum in the registered canton

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance advisory: UBO piercing analysis, PEP and sanctions screening report, and drafting of AML internal risk assessment for the low-risk standard transport business
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss-licensed legal counsel or compliance advisory firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for Stage 1 AML/CFT due diligence engagement; fixed or hourly fee structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Federal and cantonal stamp duties on incorporation (issuance tax) — no levy applicable at the CHF 100,000 minimum capital threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) and cantonal tax administration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Federal stamp duty of 1% applies only to paid-in capital exceeding CHF 1,000,000; exempt at minimum AG capital

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 626-762 (Aktiengesellschaft); Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, HRegV), Articles 15-29; the Ordinance on the Licensing of Road Transport of Persons and Goods (VPFT) for the operational licence.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Registre du commerce) of the Canton of the registered office, under supervisory authority of the Federal Office of Justice (Bundesamt für Justiz).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation together with the Articles of Association (Statuten), transmitted electronically to the Commercial Register via the unified Swiss filing platform (SoP/TEREJA) with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: CHF 100,000 minimum nominal share capital, of which at least 20% (but never less than CHF 50,000) must be paid up in cash prior to registration into a blocked escrow account (Kapitaleinlagekonto) held at a Swiss bank; the bank's certificate of escrowed funds and release undertaking is a mandatory annex to the registration filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The Board acknowledges subscription of 1,000 registered shares of CHF 100 nominal value each, fully paid into the blocked escrow account, and adopts the Articles of Association. (2) The registered office is established at [address], Canton [Zurich/Zug]. (3) The Board appoints [Name] as Chair, [Name] as Director, and [Name] as Corporate Secretary, each vested with individual signature rights. (4) The officers are authorised to complete the Commercial Register filing, publish the incorporation notice, open SWIFT and fuel-card operating accounts, and procure the international haulage licence and TIR Carnet accreditation. (5) The Board confirms the audit opt-out under article 727a(2) of the Code of Obligations and approves all ancillary filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Public notarization of the deed of incorporation and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Public Notary (Notariat) of the selected Canton (e.g., Zug or Zurich); cantonal notarial supervision office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders must appear in person before the notary or be validly represented under a notarized power of attorney. The notary verifies identity, legal capacity, the legality of the corporate purpose (cross-border bonded road freight under ISIC 5221), the share subscription plan, and the appointment of governing bodies. The deed and Articles of Association are read aloud in German (or French/Italian depending on the canton), adopted, and signed by all founders and the notary. The notary thereafter retains custody of the instrument and coordinates its transmission to the Commercial Register within three months of the deed date.
required_dossiers: Valid passports or national ID cards of all founders and directors
Swiss criminal record extract (Strafregisterauszug) of each director, issued within the last three months
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten) in the official language of the canton
Certified power of attorney if a founder is represented
Declaration of the corporate purpose and TIR/CEMT operating model
Settlement certificate for debt collection (Betreibungsregisterauszug) proving absence of pending insolvency measures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags defects (e.g., incomplete powers of attorney, inconsistent share subscription, or missing purpose clauses), the founders cure the documentation within 5 working days and re-notarize an amended deed without statutory penalty provided the 3-month filing window remains open.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Escrow deposit of minimum paid-up capital and issuance of bank attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss-regulated bank (e.g., UBS, ZKB, or a licensed cantonal bank) operating the blocked capital escrow account.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto/Kapitaleinlagekonto) in the company name. Transfer at least CHF 50,000 (20% of the CHF 100,000 nominal capital, subject to the statutory CHF 50,000 floor) in freely usable funds. The bank executes standard KYC and source-of-wealth due diligence, then issues a formal attestation (Bankbestätigung) confirming the deposit amount, the account holder, and the bank's irrevocable undertaking to release funds exclusively to the company upon presentation of the Certified Commercial Register Extract after incorporation.
required_dossiers: Funds transfer order and SWIFT confirmation for the escrowed capital
Bank KYC forms, beneficial ownership declaration (UBO), and source-of-wealth evidence
Pro-forma Articles of Association for bank file
Resolution or instruction letter from founders to open the blocked account
Bank attestation template as prescribed by HRegV
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises AML or source-of-wealth queries, submit a written source-of-funds declaration, notarized confirmation from the transferring account holder, and reasoned business plan; the attestation is ordinarily released within 10 working days of complete documentation, or the deposit is returned and another licensed bank is engaged.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial register filing, legal-entity creation, and SHAB publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt) via the electronic filing channel of the Federal Commercial Register (SoP/TEREJA) with automatic SHAB publication.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary or an authorized representative submits the notarized deed, the bank attestation, director declarations with specimen signatures, and the official registration form. The office verifies the capital rules, the legality of the articles, the directors' capacity, and the corporate seat address. Upon approval, the AG acquires legal personality and the registration is published in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce; the registrar issues the Certified Commercial Register Extract (Handelsregisterauszug) used for all downstream bank, licence, and customs steps.
required_dossiers: Notarized Deed of Incorporation and Articles of Association
Bank attestation of paid-up escrow capital
Signed specimen signatures of the Chair, Directors, and Corporate Secretary
Directors' declarations of acceptance of office and Swiss residence confirmation
Registration questionnaire with UID and seat details
Confirmation of no bankruptcy proceedings against the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a defect notice or additional-evidence inquiry, the cure period is generally 10 business days: the notary submits supplemental declarations or a corrective addendum deed; in case of substantive rejection, a fresh filing is made after rectification within the remaining validity period of the notarized deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, social insurance, and employer onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/FTA) for VAT; Central Compensation Office (ZAS) for AHV/IV/EO; SUVA for statutory accident insurance; cantonal tax office for income/capital taxation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certified Commercial Register Extract, the company automatically obtains the UID number; the directors then register the AG as a VAT taxpayer (MWST) if annual taxable turnover from transport services is projected above CHF 100,000, register as an employer with the compensation office, conclude mandatory occupational and non-occupational accident insurance with SUVA or an approved insurer, and notify the cantonal tax administration for future taxation.
required_dossiers: Certified Commercial Register Extract with UID
List of anticipated remunerations and social insurance registration forms
VAT registration form (Formulaire 03) for ESTV
Board resolution on insurance coverage and authorized bank signatories
Lease contract or title deed for the registered office
Employer labour-law questionnaire for AHV/IV/EO account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax or social insurance registrations are queried, the company submits corrected declaration of forecast turnover and payroll within 30 days; any late registration triggers only proportionate default interest and no administrative penalty where the delay is communicated proactively.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Federal Roads Office (FEDRO/ASTRA) - Road Transport Licensing Division, in conjunction with the cantonal trade and transport office for local verification; TIR guarantee authorization through SPEDLOGSWISS under the IRU guaranteeing chain.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: International Professional Goods Transport Licence (Bewilligung für gewerbsmässigen internationalen Gütertransport) under the VPFT, plus TIR Carnet Holder Accreditation and, where applicable, a CEMT multilateral quota permit for non-EU corridors.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU) and the competent Cantonal Environmental Protection Authority.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Non-EIA for pure trucking operations; mandatory Simplified Registration (Umweltverträglichkeitsprüfung light) if the operator constructs or expands a truck terminal with more than 50 heavy-vehicle parking spaces or a permanent bonded container depot exceeding 5,000 m2.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater from any maintenance or wash-bay facility must comply with the Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV) Annex 3.2: pH 6.5-9.5, COD not exceeding 60 mg/L, mineral oil hydrocarbons below 10 mg/L; VOC storage and loading emissions must respect the Clean Air Ordinance (LRV) site thresholds (e.g., solvent vapor concentration <= 150 mg/Nm3); hazardous waste (oils, filters, batteries) must be documented and removed through licensed waste operators under the Technical Ordinance on Waste (VVEA).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cantonal Fire Insurance (Gebäudeversicherung) fire-safety certification and structural load inspection of the operating depot; workplace safety clearance by SUVA/EKAS under the Swiss Accident Insurance Act (UVG), including first-aid organisation and vehicle workshop safety; FOCBS bonded-area approval for any customs warehousing premises used in TIR transits.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal Tax Administration (FTA / ESTV) — Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, Schwarztorstrasse 50, 3003 Bern; portal www.estv.admin.ch; Swiss Central Customs Directorate for TIR-related customs procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities obtain a Swiss VAT number (MWST-Nr/UID) and corporate TIN via the Federal Statistical Office once the AG is entered in the Commercial Register (Handelsregisteramt). For non-resident entities without a Swiss legal presence, direct VAT and UID registration with the FTA is mandatory for taxable activities; use Form 754 with supporting constitutive documents and appointment of a Swiss tax representative. Compliant submission to the UID register is a prerequisite before applying for TIR border-crossing permits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election under Swiss law. AG is subject to statutory corporate income tax at federal and cantonal/municipal levels. Optional elections include: federal and cantonal participation exemption for substantial dividends and capital gains; holding company or mixed company status at cantonal level; VAT fiscal unity (tax group) election for 100% affiliates; and group allocation of profits under the cantonal tax law. Hybrid mismatch rules follow OECD BEPS recommendations in Swiss tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual worldwide turnover for universal VAT liability; foreign suppliers of intangible services and e-services are subject to the same threshold on Swiss-derived turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not mandate universal e-invoicing. However, the circulation of standardized e-invoices (eBill/EX, ZUGFeRD 2.7) is recognized for VAT deduction. All customs transactions, including TIR transit and export declarations, must be transmitted electronically via the e-dec / e-vits (NCTS) system. Real-time fiscal clearance is not required, but VAT payer data must be reported electronically under the e-SAFT framework upon request.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The supply of goods is zero-rated where the goods physically leave Swiss territory (or go into a customs warehouse or free zone), and the supplier substantiates the export with customs and transport documents. Cross-border transport services (including trucking under TIR) are zero-rated when they are directly addressed to export goods, if the recipient is a taxable person abroad, or when the place of supply is outside Switzerland in accordance with the OECD place-of-consumption rules (Art. 23e Swiss VAT Act). The zero rate also applies to logistics, handling, and ancillary services that are part of the export supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (file: A/ERPDS via e-dec)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Substantiation documents must be retained for 10 years. If export zero-rating is claimed without sufficient proof at the time of the FTA audit, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 8.1% with default interest and penalties of 50% to 300% of the evaded VAT. Intentional evasion triggers criminal fines up to CHF 250,000 and imprisonment terms under Swiss VAT Act Art. 91; fraudulent TIR transactions additionally are referred to the Federal Office of Customs and Border Security and to the jurisdiction of the criminal courts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) — Schweizerische Nationalbank / Banque nationale suisse / Banca nazionale svizzera, Berne and Zurich; jointly with the Swiss Federal Department of Finance (FDF) administering the Federal Act on Currency and Payment Instruments (CPIA) and banking ordinances. The SNB is the sole issuer of banknotes and operator of the Swiss Interbank Clearing (SIC) system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland maintains a fully liberalised currency regime: the Swiss franc (CHF) is freely convertible on both current and capital account, with no foreign exchange control law, no central bank approval requirement for cross-border payments, and no restrictions on inbound capital, profit repatriation, or dividend remittance to non-residents. Legal tender status of CHF is defined under the CPIA, but payment in foreign currency is contractually permissible. The sole practical obstacle to remittance of distributable profits is the 35% federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends and similar distributions, which is refundable upon recipient tax residency disclosure or reducible to the applicable double tax treaty rate; no additional cantonal or federal FX or transfer permit is required. For a TIR bond-carrying trucking AG, fuel and toll expenses incurred in EUR and other currencies are freely payable; hedge accounting and foreign-currency bank balances are unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Swiss law imposes no statutory surrender or repatriation requirement on export proceeds, no mandatory conversion into CHF, and no time limit for the holding of foreign currency receipts. Exporters operating under TIR carnets may retain EUR, USD, or CHF balances in domestic or foreign banks, apply them directly to outbound trade payments, or convert at market rates. Switzerland's only residual control is the obligation to truthfully declare cross-border cash movements of CHF 10,000 or more to customs authorities pursuant to the Money Laundering Act, which applies to physical cash, not wire transfers.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (payment clearing and fuel card settlement)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for core treasury, Medium for ancillary rails. Offshore digital e-money institutions (EMIs) are not regulated by FINMA and cannot hold statutory capital escrow, issue Swiss IBAN accounts, or provide SIC access; they operate only under acquiring or partner-bank arrangements and are acceptable solely as supplementary fuel-card or wage-distribution channels. Domestic Swiss FinTech licensees under the Banking Act (FinTech licence, public deposits up to CHF 100 million without interest or securities business) and licensed payment service providers may provide operational accounts, but a full banking relationship with a SIC participant remains mandatory for a TIR trucking AG's primary settlement and commercial credit needs. Use of any non-FINMA-regulated EMI for statutory shareholder capital injection would be rejected by the Swiss Commercial Register office and notaries.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory in practice. Swiss banks uniformly require at least one natural-person signatory, typically a managing director or beneficial owner with Swiss residence or an authorised Swiss-based representative, to appear physically before a relationship manager or a Swiss notary; fully remote video-only onboarding is not accepted for corporate accounts of foreign-owned AGs except for very low-value prepaid wallets, which are irrelevant for treasury. Where all directors are non-resident, the bank mandates a personal interview at the Swiss head office or a recognised Swiss embassy/consulate, supplemented by original apostilled constitutional documents. Non-compliance with this interview mandate is an automatic onboarding blocker; escrow accounts for share capital specifically require notarised confirmation of the payor mandate (Einzahlungsschein) and a bank confirmation of the blocked deposit before the Commercial Register filing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque beneficial ownership or suspicion of bearer-share structure; nominee directors or fiduciary shareholding without disclosed economic owner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Official Swiss Commercial Register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) dated within 90 days; current articles of association; Form A (Swiss entity beneficial owner declaration) or Form B (non-Swiss entity) as per Swiss Bankers Association KYC guidelines; complete structured ownership chart identifying all natural persons above 25%; notarised declaration of beneficial ownership; audited annual financial statements or opening balance sheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Lack of operational substance in Switzerland; letterbox company risk; unverifiable cross-border trucking activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validly signed warehouse or registered office lease; Swiss payroll records and social security (AHV/SUVA) confirmation for Swiss staff; FEDRO (Federal Roads Office) licence for international commercial transport; TIR Carnet holder certificate issued by the Swiss automobile club or authorised guaranteeing association; professional liability and cargo insurance policies; vehicle fleet registration documents (Swiss or foreign) and telematics/route logs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, politically exposed person status, or adverse media against ultimate beneficial owners or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed bank's sanctioned-party screening declarations; PEP self-declaration for each beneficial owner and signatory; sworn source-of-funds statement with supporting bank statements, sale contracts, inheritance/gift instruments or dividend vouchers; independent negative-news due diligence report from a licensed provider; commitment letter for ongoing transaction monitoring compliance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-intensive or otherwise high-risk transaction profile typical of fuel purchases, border tolls, and subcontractor settlements, particularly in CIS / Middle East corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Digital fuel-card clearing statements (e.g., DKV, UTA, Routex) evidencing non-cash settlement; signed subcontractor agreements with VAT and customs declarations; LSVA (heavy vehicle road charge) statements; TIR carnet discharge certificates (carnet receipts); itemised export/import customs declarations; 12-month historical transaction analysis; anti-cash payment policy certified by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inward shareholder loan or capital injection from jurisdictions with heightened monitoring or from non-bank lenders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial deed of capital increase; board resolution approving the capital call; shareholder bank account statements evidencing legitimate origin; Swiss Commercial Register filing confirmation after escrow release; intercompany loan agreement in writing with arm's length interest and repayment schedule; Swiss stamp duty (emissions tax) declaration on paid-up capital by 31 March of the following year.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing of the minimum registered capital (CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 fully paid at formation) is executed by domestic SWIFT MT103 payment to a Swiss SIC-participant bank's blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) designated for capital formation. The remittance must reference the company's Commercial Register file number and be accompanied by an Einzahlungsschein (payment certificate) naming each subscribing shareholder and the precise CHF amount. Banks require the payer (ultimate beneficial owner) to match the notarised subscription declaration; third-party payments are prohibited. For post-formation inbound share premium, shareholder loans, or intercompany advances, use SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose codes 'DETI' (equity injection) or 'DISA' (direct investment in non-financial enterprise); after receipt, present the bank's confirmation to the notary and the Commercial Register office. The bank must verify no cash, no commingled funds, and a clear audit trail from the shareholder's bank account; escrow release occurs only upon registration of the AG. For funds arriving in EUR or USD, conversion to CHF is executed at the bank's published spot rate; no SNB approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Swiss treasury clearing rails for a TIR trucking AG comprise: (i) domestic CHF disbursements via SIC instant or batch clearing with ISO 20022 pain.001 messages; (ii) euro-denominated settlements via SEPA Credit Transfer from a Swiss SEPA participant bank, using the same IBAN/BIC corridor; (iii) non-SEPA cross-border trade payments, fuel-card top-ups, and subcontractor settlements via SWIFT MT103 with full purpose code and supporting customs/TIR references; and (iv) documentary trade instruments for fleet and capital equipment purchases through irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued by MT700 to the beneficiary's bank, frequently on 90-day usance terms. TIR carnets themselves are discharged through the guaranteeing association rather than the clearing system; LSVA tolls are debited directly via SEPA direct debit or fuel-card networks. CHF/EUR conversion for euro corridor expenditures is consolidated through standing FX conversion orders to minimise spread. All outbound disbursements above CHF 15,000 require stated purpose codes and, where triggered, underlying invoice/contract storage to satisfy Swiss bank re-verification duties under the AMLA; payments to subcontractors abroad must be accompanied by properly executed consignment and customs records to avoid unjust enrichment claims and maintain bonded cargo compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards in CHF/EUR and CHF/USD for up to 12 months, commonly executed under a bank master FX agreement without ISDA
FX swaps (swap contre change) for simultaneous spot-forward restructuring of EUR and CHF liquidity, permitted for cash-flow matching of fuel, toll, and payroll cycles
Cross-currency swaps (currency interest rate swaps) under ISDA/CSA for long-term financing alignment on asset-backed fleet loans

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on currencies without SNB-issued freely deliverable CHR reference, but only with a FINMA-regulated counterparty and strictly for hedging genuine TIR corridor operating exposure (e.g., RUB, TRY, KZT)
European-style EUR/USD futures listed on NYSE Euronext or Eurex for anticipatory hedging of intermodal revenue, settled in cash

FX options (plain vanilla call/put) for asymmetric protection on large capital expenditures, permissible without SNB notification; speculative option writing on the corporate account is prohibited by Swiss banking practice and would breach the company's treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, directors' report, AGM approval and profit appropriation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' meeting; signed originals kept at registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after balance sheet date (Art. 699 Code of Obligations), unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered dissolution if the AGM is not held; civil liability of board for missing accounts and unpaid distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal, cantonal and communal corporate income and capital tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration and Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally six months after fiscal year-end; extension to 12 months available on application, subject to canton-specific deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest on unpaid tax, late-filing procedural fines, and assessment by estimation in case of non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Status-defined quarterly, annual or monthly basis; generally due within 60 days after close of each VAT period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT default interest and late-payment interest, penalty up to the tax at risk, collection enforcement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual social security wage declaration and AHV contribution statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 January following the payroll year or earlier deadline set by the compensation office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest, contribution arrears, administrative fines and possible criminal sanctions for false declarations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary statutory audit mandatory when an Aktiengesellschaft exceeds two of three thresholds for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total over CHF 20 million, net turnover over CHF 40 million, or more than 250 full-time employees. Listed companies and certain high-risk licensed entities require ordinary audit irrespective of thresholds. Companies with 10 or fewer full-time employees may opt out of the limited audit by unanimous shareholder consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss Code of Obligations accounting provisions; Swiss GAAP FER or IFRS may be adopted and is mandatory for securities-listed and certain group-reporting entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No recurring public UBO or annual confirmation filing is submitted to the Commercial Register in Switzerland. The AG must maintain an internal register of beneficial owners on a current basis; registered share transfers are entered in the Aktienbuch immediately upon occurrence. The board's annual presentation of the share register to the AGM serves as the de facto annual confirmation for shareholding transfers. Bearer shares, if issued, require advance identification of beneficial owners before voting rights are exercised.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (board and shareholders' meeting minutes)
Beneficial ownership register, if bearer shares are outstanding

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600–2,500 per year for a registered office plus corporate secretarial/fiduciary services, depending on canton and scope
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500–8,000 for a limited review; USD 5,000–18,000 for an ordinary statutory audit, depending on group complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% statutory Swiss federal corporate income tax rate (effective federal rate approx. 7.83% after deduction of the federal tax itself); combined federal + cantonal + communal ordinary AG burden in Zug approx. 11.5%–11.9%
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: STAF 2020 regime: full participation relief (Beteiligungsabzug) on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income from holdings of at least 10%; patent box limiting effective taxation of qualifying IP income to approximately 10%; additional R&D deduction of 50% of qualifying Swiss R&D expenses; notional interest deduction available in certain cantons, supplementary depreciation on movable assets for transportation fleets; no statutory tax holidays for ordinary AGs

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Swiss corporate income tax return for legal persons (Steuererklärung juristische Personen / Form A) filed through the competent cantonal tax administration (in Zug: Steuerverwaltung des Kantons Zug); electronic filing via ESTV e-Steuer platform, SwissTax desktop/cloud software, or the Zug cantonal e-filing portal; federal taxes (Direkte Bundessteuer) are assessed in the same federal/cantonal combined procedure
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual filing; quarterly advance payments of federal, cantonal and communal income taxes and capital tax are made during the tax period; separate quarterly or semi-annual Swiss VAT (MWST) returns apply if the trucking entity is VAT-registered
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Cantonal filing notice normally requires submission within 6 months after the fiscal year-end (for a 31 December year-end: by 30 June of the following year); the Federal Tax Administration may set an independent federal deadline; extensions up to 12 months are obtainable on reasoned application, particularly for cross-border groups; a final default assessment (Ermessensveranlagung) may be issued if the return is not filed within the granted term

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered and legal company name, registered seat (domicile), registered office address, UID number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx), and Swiss Commercial Register data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Swiss AG's exact registered seat (e.g., Zug, canton Zug); foreign controlling shareholders are identified in the ownership schedule; every change of directors or domicile affecting treaty access must be reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of the tax period (fiscal year; normally the calendar year for an AG unless a different business year is approved).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm the fiscal year-end; align the period with the foreign parent's consolidated audit cycle and transfer pricing documentation year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Names of statutory directors, members of the executive body, and the audit firm; disclosure of persons authorised to sign for the company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose the non-resident directors and Swiss resident operational managers; the TIR licensing and the transport permit (Bewilligung für gewerbsmässigen Strassengütertransport) must be held by the Swiss AG and named in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Share capital, statutory reserves, voluntary reserves, and capital contribution reserves (Kapitaleinlagereserven); confirms minimum capital compliance for the AG (CHF 100,000 authorised, CHF 50,000 paid).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report shareholder loans and intercompany balances; excessive debt or interest on shareholder loans is subject to thin-capitalisation treatment and reclassification into taxable distributions. Ensure capital contribution reserves are evidenced by Swiss filing documentation; otherwise distributions may be reclassified as taxable dividends with 35% withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit: accounting profit per statutory income statement adjusted for non-deductible expenses, tax-accepted depreciation, provisions, and participation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: TIR and bonded freight revenues must be classified per source; income derived by the Swiss AG is taxable on a worldwide basis unless allocated to a foreign permanent establishment or properly excluded under the applicable DTA. Include truck depreciation, fuel costs, TIR carnet guarantee fees, salaries, and insurance; add back non-deductible Swiss withholding tax on deemed profit bars? and any fines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from shareholdings of at least 10% or minimum holding value; applies participation deduction with the corresponding pro-rata financing expense disallowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign parent should use a Swiss holding or subholding structure only if the participation is held for genuine business reasons; participation relief will be denied for shell structures without substance. The shares must be booked as fixed financial assets, and holding periods must satisfy the statutory thresholds. All source-country withholding tax should be grossed up and segregated on the WHT reconciliation schedule for DTA credit claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use of loss carryforwards: losses from prior business years (up to 7 years per Art. 67 of the Federal Tax Act) are deducted from the current net profit of the same taxpayer before calculation of federal tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign permanent establishment may not offset Swiss-source income unless the applicable DTA permits a Swiss taxpayer to deduct them; ring-fence TIR route losses by permanent establishment and verify the 7-year forfeiture is monitored per jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reported taxable equity for cantonal capital tax (Kapitalsteuer), composed of paid-up share capital and disclosed reserves; object of the cantonal/municipal capital tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany financing of the trucking fleet through shareholder loans increases the capital tax base if booked as reserves; covenant and substance documentation must match the share-capital registration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Voluntary annex listing fleet assets, TIR carnet guarantees involving IRU, border-crossing authorisations, diesel excise refunds, and VAT recovery structures used for long-haul operations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Swiss AG operating TIR trucking, provide per-vehicle and per-route profitability data in the income-tax reconciliation; cross-border freight under TIR must be separated from cabotage and domestic Swiss transport, which are fully taxable in Switzerland; document any access to Swiss VAT refund schemes for fuel and motorway vignettes.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing: formal reminder and disciplinary fine (Verfahrensstrafe) of CHF 100 up to CHF 10,000 under Article 174 DBG; statutory default interest on assessed tax; default assessment at an inflated amount (Ermessensveranlagung) is subject to review and surcharges; late-payment interest under cantonal law accrues from 30 days after the assessment; deliberate omission leading to underestimation of tax is treated as tax evasion with a fine up to the evaded tax amount, tripled in aggravated cases; directors and legal representatives are liable for procedural fines of the company.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) on dividends paid out of Swiss movable capital; no additional cantonal/communal withholding tax. The 35% withholding is refunded to Swiss resident shareholders and reduced under DTA for non-residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must submit a DTA preferential withholding tax relief application to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), typically using the Swiss extra-cantonal refund form accompanying the dividend, within 3 years from the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became payable. The applicant must provide: (i) an original tax residence certificate (TRC) from its country of residence issued by the competent foreign tax authority; (ii) declaration of beneficial ownership; (iii) confirmation that the Swiss dividend was reported in the foreign tax return; and (iv) any DTA-specific condition (e.g., an effective 10% or 25% shareholding, holding period of at least 6 or 12 months, real economic substance of the foreign recipient). For dividends not covered by a DTA, the withholding tax remains at 35%; refunds are governed by the general decree of the Federal Council. In respect of the Swiss AG itself, any dividend received from a foreign subsidiary is subject to Swiss 35% withholding only if paid via a Swiss payment agent; under participation relief, the dividend received is effectively tax-free after the reserve condition is met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Switzerland does not impose statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties (licence fees) or on ordinary commercial intercompany interest; interest on Swiss bonds, debentures or similar treasury obligations is subject to 35% withholding tax; interest on bank deposits and commercial accounts in the name of Swiss financial institutions is generally outside withholding. Under most Swiss DTAs: royalties 0% at source; interest 0–10% (commonly 0% for banking interest and 5% for bond interest); the standard preferential dividend rate under DTAs into Switzerland is 15% for portfolio shareholdings and 5% for holdings of at least 10%; several treaties (e.g., with the Netherlands plus certain old Germany, Austria and UK-bound treaty positions) provide a 0% holding-company dividend rate subject to substance and 80% participation-anticipation thresholds. Treaty benefits are denied under the OECD BEPS Principal Purpose Test (PPT) where the arrangement lacks genuine commercial substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CHF 10,000,000 (annual aggregate of cross-border intercompany transactions) is the de facto threshold derived from Swiss Federal Tax Administration audit practice requiring contemporaneous Transfer Pricing Documentation (Local File); intra-group service charges exceeding CHF 2,000,000 trigger functional and cost-benefit analysis documentation; a Master File should be prepared for MNE groups with consolidated turnover above CHF 1,000,000,000, aligning with OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines. Switzerland imposes no statutory TP filing obligation but documentation must be submitted within 60 days of tax-administration demand; burden of proof for arm's-length compliance shifts on failure to provide documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland enforces economic substance through (i) substantive anti-abuse doctrine under Article 6 of the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax allowing disregardia of artificial arrangements; (ii) the OECD Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) minimum standards, including the Principal Purpose Test in all Swiss DTAs concluded or modified after 2024; (iii) the Swiss STAF 2020 requirement that treaty benefits, participation relief, and patent box apply only to an enterprise with genuine economic activity, own premises, qualified employees and business decision-making in Switzerland; and (iv) the OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) anti-abuse rules. A Swiss AG acting as a pure invoicing or letterbox vehicle for TIR foreign transport operations without Swiss operational activity will be reassessed as having a permanent establishment abroad or a permanent establishment in Switzerland and the nominal Swiss entity will be denied treaty benefits and may be liquidated for non-compliance with the TIR licensing requirement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a Swiss corporate tax return containing knowingly false, incomplete or misleading statements (e.g., understating TIR freight revenue, inflating fuel deductions, failing to declare foreign bank accounts of the Swiss AG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine under Art. 175 of the Federal Act on Direct Federal Tax up to the tax evaded; in aggravated cases (Art. 176, e.g., repeated evasion or false documents of substantial scale) a fine up to three times the evaded tax; VAT evasion under the Swiss VAT Act carries comparable penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and executive officers who knowingly participated in the evasion are personally criminally liable; additionally, joint and several civil liability to the corporation under articles 752–754 of the Swiss Code of Obligations; recovery actions may target personal bank accounts; revocation of the vehicle operating licence and prohibition on maintaining residence in Switzerland are possible measures in the context of major VAT and fuel-excise fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of forged commercial documents, altered TIR carnets, counterfeit customs declarations, false import/export invoices, or creation of sham suppliers for diesel and toll costs to suppress taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Custodial sentence of up to three years, or monetary penalty for negligent commission, under the Swiss Criminal Code and the customs and tax legislation; confiscation of vehicles, fuel stock and criminal assets; exclusion from Swiss public procurement; per route, the customs evasion fine may reach five times the duties evaded plus the payable duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal imprisonment, travel bans within Switzerland pending extradition cooperation, and civil restitution orders; the corporate veil is pierced for fraud to attach the assets of the signatory directors and beneficial owners; European arrest warrant and Interpol red notices may issue for cross-border TIR offences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of a Swiss AG that is a pure domiciliary entity without employees, premises, operating assets or business decisions in Switzerland, interposed solely to route TIR invoices and obtain DTA withholding relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the artificial structure under Art. 6 DBG; denial of participation relief and treaty refunds; assessment at the place of effective management (often the foreign seat of the parent); 5% deemed profit uplift plus penalties; annulment of the holding privilege and possible revocation of the TIR transport licence by the Swiss federal office of transport if the entity is no longer the operator.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing director and each director residing in Switzerland are jointly liable for the unpaid taxes and penalties; foreign directors may be subject to Swiss administrative assistance requests with criminal referral; personal bank guarantees and director liability policies are often void in cases of deliberately abusive structures.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Non-Remittance of Withholding Tax and Social Contributions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring profits and distributing dividends without withholding and remitting the 35% Swiss withholding tax; failing to withhold and remit employee and driver social security contributions (AHV/ALV/UV) and source taxes on salaries of foreign truck drivers working under the Swiss AG.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Mandatory simple interest on outstanding withholding tax; negligence penalty of up to 20% of the unremitted tax; deliberate evasion from withholding tax payment increases the penalty to three times the evaded amount; social security contributions carry contribution surcharges and administrative fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Article 37 of the Federal Withholding Tax Act imposes direct personal liability on statutory representatives and managing officers of the company for unrecovered withholding tax; civil liability and criminal fines at personal level; travel restrictions are common in cross-border transport cases where directors are non-residents; social security collection authorities may enforce against the private assets of directors who signed the payroll.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering, AML and Customs/TIR Fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Swiss AG or its Swiss bank accounts to launder proceeds from customs smuggling, diesel excise fraud, illegal cabotage or rapid-turnover fictitious fuel card invoicing; knowingly receiving inflated fuel-card or freight invoices from related entities; failure to perform beneficial-owner due diligence in cash-intensive border stops.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss Criminal Code Art. 305bis money laundering: custodial sentence up to three years and a fine; aggravated laundering (professional/band) up to five years; failure to report to the Money-Laundering Reporting Office Switzerland (Art. 305ter) or negligence in the banking-AML context leads to fines and closure of bank mandates; customs offences under Art. 118 of the Swiss Customs Act: repayment of duties, confiscation, penalty up to the amount evaded and, in serious cases, disqualification from TIR guaranteeing procedures.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are individually criminally liable; corporate bank guarantees are frozen by the reporting obligation; personal travel bans and asset freezes are available under Swiss legal assistance; the corporate veil is pierced for civil recovery of the laundering proceeds; for foreign beneficial owners, extradition to the protected state of the laundering offence is maintained under Swiss extradition law; the TIR guarantee chain (IRU/ATIT) may seek indemnification from the directors' personal assets under guarantee agreements.
